# lgtmaybe — full documentation

> AI code review for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Azure DevOps, and local Git diffs. It posts inline findings and a summary on pull and merge requests, or prints findings locally. Choose from seven hosted providers, ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure support keyless cloud auth.

Source: https://lgtmaybe.coles.codes/ — generated from the docs/ tree.

---

<!-- Source: https://lgtmaybe.coles.codes/ -->

<div class="hero" markdown>

![lgtmaybe logo: a shrugging face with curly-brace arms](assets/logo.svg){ width="128" }

# lgtmaybe

</div>

lgtmaybe reviews pull and merge requests on **GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, and Azure
DevOps**, posting inline comments and one summary. Choose a hosted model,
ollama, or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

It works before a pull request exists. Run `lgtmaybe review` on your
branch, add a [pre-commit hook](how-to/review-before-you-commit.md), or
[hand its findings to your coding agent](how-to/fix-findings-with-an-ai-agent.md)
to fix. With a local model, your code stays local.

It reads the diff plus a little surrounding code and comments only on changed
lines. It never checks out or runs the change, skips generated files and
binaries, [redacts](reference/glossary.md#redaction) secrets, and treats
author-supplied text as untrusted.

It checks for:

- **Correctness and security:** logic errors, missed `await`s, injection, auth mistakes, and leaked secrets.
- **Code health:** performance problems, needless complexity, deprecations, and risky dependencies.
- **Tests and documentation:** missing or weak tests, stale comments, and undocumented APIs.
- **Intent:** whether the change does what its title, description, and commits say.
- **Ponytail:** code you don't need, and simpler or standard-library ways to do the job.
- **Architecture:** coupling, wrong-way dependencies, and broken subclass contracts that will be hard to undo.

Each [finding](reference/glossary.md#finding) is graded `info` to `critical`
and lands on its changed line. A clean change gets a 👍 **LGTM!**.

![An inline lgtmaybe comment flagging a critical SQL injection and suggesting a fix](assets/marketplace/marketplace-screenshot-1.png){ width="720" }

Slash commands refresh a review (`/review`, `/improve`), answer a question
(`/ask`), or post a description (`/describe`) or
[change overview](how-to/generate-a-change-diagram.md) (`/diagram`). The
overview rates the risk of change, lists high-impact areas, and draws a
flowchart, plus a sequence diagram when the change alters a runtime flow.
`lgtmaybe diagram` prints a text version locally.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    web["Storefront<br/>React<br/>places orders"]
    api["Order API<br/>Python<br/>creates orders (changed)"]
    db["Order database<br/>PostgreSQL<br/>stores orders"]
    queue["Order events<br/>SQS<br/>buffers events (new)"]
    worker["Notification worker<br/>Python<br/>sends confirmations (new)"]
    email["Email provider<br/>delivers messages"]
    web -->|calls| api
    api -->|stores in| db
    api -->|publishes to| queue
    queue -->|delivers to| worker
    worker -->|sends via| email
```

## What's New

## Providers

| Provider | Auth |
|---|---|
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `zai` | `ZAI_API_KEY` for GLM / Zhipu AI; optional `--api-base` for the China / coding-plan endpoint |
| `bedrock` | Ambient AWS creds via GitHub OIDC, no static key |
| `vertex` | Ambient GCP creds via Workload Identity Federation, no key |
| `azure` | Resource endpoint, plus `AZURE_API_KEY` or keyless Entra (Azure AD) creds via GitHub OIDC |
| `ollama` | None: local only, zero cost |
| `openai-compatible` | `--api-base` to any OpenAI `/v1` endpoint; key optional (placeholder for keyless local servers) |

<!-- Source: https://lgtmaybe.coles.codes/tutorial/getting-started/ -->

# Getting Started with lgtmaybe

This tutorial walks you through your first review using **ollama**. ollama runs
the model on your own machine, costs nothing, and needs no API keys. By the end
you will have reviewed a branch and seen the findings in your terminal. You need
no GitHub token and no pull request.

Two words first:

- A [finding](../reference/glossary.md#finding) is one issue the review
  reports. It has a [severity](../reference/glossary.md#severity), a title and
  an explanation, and sometimes a suggested fix.
- A [lens](../reference/glossary.md#lens) is one focused review question, such
  as "is this secure?". lgtmaybe runs several lenses and merges their findings.

## What You Need

- Python 3.11 or later
- [ollama](https://ollama.com) running locally
- A local git repository with some changes on a branch to review

## Step 1: Install lgtmaybe

```bash
pip install lgtmaybe
```

On macOS you can install from the Homebrew tap instead:

```bash
brew tap MattJColes/tap
brew trust MattJColes/tap   # current Homebrew requires trusting third-party taps
brew install lgtmaybe
```

[Install the CLI](../how-to/install-the-cli.md) explains three things: the
`brew trust` step, the Windows (WinGet) install, and which providers the base
install covers. API-key and local providers work out of the box. Keyless cloud
providers need a `pip` extra.

Verify the install:

```bash
lgtmaybe --help
```

## Step 2: Start ollama and Pull a Model

```bash
ollama serve          # starts the local server on http://localhost:11434
ollama pull qwen3.6:27b   # or any model you prefer
```

Leave `ollama serve` running in a separate terminal.

## Step 3: Point lgtmaybe at ollama

lgtmaybe has no built-in model, so tell it once which provider and model to
use:

```bash
lgtmaybe config init
```

It finds the running ollama and the models you have pulled, so you only
confirm:

```console
Found ollama running at http://localhost:11434 (1 model pulled) - use ollama? [Y/n]:
Pulled models: qwen3.6:27b
Model [qwen3.6:27b]:
Checking ollama / qwen3.6:27b with one short request...
OK: the model answered.
Wrote /home/you/.config/lgtmaybe/config.yml
Next: lgtmaybe review
```

Press Enter twice. Before it writes anything, it sends the model one tiny
request. A stopped server or a model you have not pulled fails here, not
halfway through a review.

The file holds only the provider and model. If you later use a hosted provider,
its API key stays in your environment.

If ollama is on another machine, answer `n`, choose `ollama`, and enter its
address. You can also skip `config init` and pass `--provider ollama --model
qwen3.6:27b` to each command. Without either, `lgtmaybe review` stops straight
away and tells you to run `config init`.

## Step 4: Review Your Changes

From inside a git repo, on a branch with some changes, run:

```bash
lgtmaybe review
```

lgtmaybe diffs your current branch against the remote primary branch. It tries
`origin/HEAD` first, then falls back to `origin/main` / `origin/master`, then a
local `main` / `master`. It sends the diff, with some surrounding lines for
context, to your local qwen3.6:27b model. Then it prints the findings to your
terminal:

```console
src/app.py:14  [MEDIUM] Missing None check before use (confidence 8/10)
  find_user() returns None for an unknown id, so user.email raises AttributeError.

1 finding · risk low (no risk signals) · provider ollama · model qwen3.6:27b · lgtmaybe 2.11.1
```

Each finding shows its file and line, severity and title, then the explanation.
The last line does three things:

- counts the findings
- rates the [risk of the change](../reference/glossary.md#risk-of-change)
- names the model and lgtmaybe version

Three flags change what gets reviewed:

- `--working` reviews the whole worktree (your branch's commits plus
  uncommitted edits).
- `--uncommitted` reviews only the uncommitted edits.
- `--base main` diffs against a different base.

`lgtmaybe review --help` lists the everyday options. `--help-all` adds the
advanced tuning ones.

## Step 5: Change the Output Format

`--format` controls what `review` prints. `--json` (shorthand for
`--format json`) emits a JSON array ready to pipe into other tooling:

```bash
lgtmaybe review --json
```

`--format agent` prints the findings as correction instructions that an AI
coding agent can read and apply. Use it for a local review-and-fix loop. See
[Fix findings with an AI agent](../how-to/fix-findings-with-an-ai-agent.md).

`--format sarif` prints a [SARIF](../reference/glossary.md#sarif) 2.1.0 log.
You can upload it to GitHub code scanning or open it in an IDE. See
[Upload findings as SARIF](../how-to/upload-findings-as-sarif.md).

## Step 6: See the Whole Change

`lgtmaybe diagram` sends the same local diff to three concurrent model calls.
It prints the
[**change overview**](../reference/glossary.md#change-overview):

- a description of what you changed
- a risk-of-change rating (computed locally, no model call)
- a [**High Impact Areas**](../reference/glossary.md#high-impact-areas) section
  calling out anything that could bite, such as infrastructure, security
  posture, outage risk, migrations, or backups
- a diagram of the components your change touches, plus a sequence diagram
  when it alters a run-time flow

```bash
lgtmaybe diagram
```

It takes the same `--base` / `--working` / `--uncommitted` flags as `review`.

Run `review` then `diagram` before you open a pull request. The first tells you
what's wrong with the change. The second tells you what the change is and what
it could break.

The diagrams print as Mermaid source plus a text rendering for the terminal.
Paste the Mermaid into a GitHub comment or [mermaid.live](https://mermaid.live)
to see it drawn. See
[Generate a change overview](../how-to/generate-a-change-diagram.md).

## Step 7: Post Reviews on Real Pull Requests

The CLI reviews local changes. To post inline comments and a summary on real
pull requests, wire lgtmaybe into your code host. The review is the same on
every host; only the setup differs:

- **GitHub:** add the Action to your repo.
  See [Use as a GitHub Action](../how-to/use-as-github-action.md).
- **GitLab:** add a CI job.
  See [Review on GitLab](../how-to/review-on-gitlab.md).
- **Gitea:** add a Gitea Actions workflow.
  See [Review on Gitea](../how-to/review-on-gitea.md).
- **Azure DevOps:** add an Azure Pipelines build validation policy.
  See [Review on Azure DevOps](../how-to/review-on-azure-devops.md).

## What Happened Under the Hood

lgtmaybe ran its pipeline over your local diff:

1. **Fetch:** read the diff from your local repo with `git`.
2. **Filter:** skipped generated files, binaries, and lockfiles. It
   [redacted](../reference/glossary.md#redaction) anything that looked like a
   secret.
3. **Review:** sent five concurrent model calls, one per concern: security,
   correctness, code health, artefacts (tests and documentation), and
   architecture. This is the default `fast`
   [preset](../reference/glossary.md#preset). Each call asked for findings as
   JSON.
4. **Parse and anchor:** validated each reply against the findings schema. It
   pinned every finding to the changed line it quotes (its
   [anchor](../reference/glossary.md#anchor)).
5. **Reflect:** asked the model to audit its own findings
   ([reflection](../reference/glossary.md#reflection)). It dropped the ones the
   model could not stand behind.
6. **Filter findings:** dropped defect findings with no concrete failure
   scenario. It also dropped anything below the severity floor (`low` by
   default).
7. **Render:** printed the findings. The GitHub Action posts them to the pull
   request instead.

## Next Steps

- To configure severity thresholds, path filters, and token caps, see
  [Configure .lgtmaybe.yml](../how-to/configure-lgtmaybe-yml.md).
- To use a cloud provider with no API keys, see
  [Review with Bedrock OIDC](../how-to/review-with-bedrock-oidc.md) or
  [Review with Vertex WIF](../how-to/review-with-vertex-wif.md).
- To use lgtmaybe in a GitHub Actions workflow, see
  [Use as a GitHub Action](../how-to/use-as-github-action.md).

# Install the CLI

Install the `lgtmaybe` command-line tool once, then point it at any provider.
This page covers getting the CLI onto your machine. Choosing a model backend (a
hosted API, keyless cloud, or a local model) comes after: see the
[provider how-tos](../index.md#providers) and
[Choose a review model](choose-a-review-model.md).

## Install (pip)

Works on any OS with Python 3.11+:

```bash
pip install lgtmaybe
```

Verify it:

```bash
lgtmaybe --help
```

That prints the command list with usage examples. `<command> --help` lists a
command's options. For `lgtmaybe review` it shows only the everyday ones and
ends with a line pointing at `lgtmaybe review --help-all`, which lists the
advanced tuning options too.

To check which build you are running, for a bug report or a benchmark record:

```bash
lgtmaybe --version
```

It prints one line, `lgtmaybe <version>`, for every install method (pip,
Homebrew, or the Windows executable). A source checkout that was never
installed has no version metadata and prints `lgtmaybe unknown`.

Upgrade later with `pip install --upgrade lgtmaybe`.

## Install on Windows (WinGet)

The WinGet package is a portable executable for Windows x86_64 (64-bit).
Install it by its exact package identifier:

```powershell
winget install --id MattJColes.lgtmaybe --exact
```

Verify the command alias:

```powershell
lgtmaybe --help
```

Upgrade or uninstall it later with the same package identifier:

```powershell
winget upgrade --id MattJColes.lgtmaybe --exact
winget uninstall --id MattJColes.lgtmaybe --exact
```

If WinGet cannot find a newly published version, refresh its package sources
and retry:

```powershell
winget source update
```

The executable bundles ast-grep for cross-file symbol resolution. It does not
bundle the optional cloud SDKs for keyless Bedrock, Vertex, or Azure, so use
pip with the matching extra for those providers (see
[below](#cloud-providers-need-extras)). `pip install lgtmaybe` also works on
Windows.

## Install on macOS (Homebrew)

On macOS (and Linuxbrew) you can install from the project's
[Homebrew tap](https://github.com/MattJColes/homebrew-tap) instead of `pip`:

```bash
brew tap MattJColes/tap
brew trust MattJColes/tap
brew install lgtmaybe
```

The middle step is required. Current Homebrew refuses to load a formula from a
third-party tap until you explicitly **trust** it (`Error: Refusing to load
formula … from untrusted tap`). You decide this once per machine, for every tap
outside Homebrew's core, and a tap author cannot waive it for you. To trust
only this formula instead of the whole tap, use
`brew trust --formula MattJColes/tap/lgtmaybe`.

`brew install MattJColes/tap/lgtmaybe` taps and installs in one line, but still
needs the `brew trust` step first or it stops at the untrusted-tap error.

Upgrade later with `brew upgrade lgtmaybe`.

If you tapped the earlier `MattJColes/lgtmaybe` name, switch over once with
`brew untap MattJColes/lgtmaybe && brew tap MattJColes/tap`, then
`brew trust MattJColes/tap`. Upgrades keep working on the old tap because GitHub
redirects the renamed repo, so switching is optional tidying.

Homebrew installs lgtmaybe into its own virtualenv, so it never touches your
system or project Python. The formula installs lgtmaybe and its dependencies
from prebuilt **PyPI wheels** (no compiling), so a first install takes about a
minute, mostly download time. There is no prebuilt bottle, so it works on any
architecture and macOS version. It also installs the `ast-grep` formula, which
lgtmaybe uses for cross-file symbol resolution.

## Cloud Providers Need Extras

The base pip install, Homebrew formula, and Windows executable cover every
API-key and local provider:

| Providers | Covered by base install? |
|---|---|
| `openai`, `anthropic`, `openrouter`, `zai`: set the provider's API key in your environment | ✅ Yes |
| `ollama`, `openai-compatible`: point `--api-base` at the server (local, or a hosted OpenAI-compatible API) | ✅ Yes |
| `bedrock`, `vertex`, `azure`: keyless cloud (OIDC/WIF) | ❌ Needs an extra |

The keyless cloud providers need cloud SDKs that the Homebrew formula and
Windows executable do not bundle. Install the CLI from PyPI with the matching
extra:

```bash
pip install 'lgtmaybe[bedrock]'   # or [vertex] / [azure]
```

Or run them through the [GitHub Action](use-as-github-action.md), whose image
bundles all three SDKs and handles the OIDC/WIF exchange for you.

To use `--static-analysis` locally, install the tools it drives with
`pip install 'lgtmaybe[static-analysis]'` (ruff, bandit, mypy, semgrep, and
zizmor). gitleaks and osv-scanner are separate binaries you install yourself;
any tool that is not installed is skipped. The Action image bundles all of
them.

To serve reviews to a coding agent with `lgtmaybe mcp`, install the MCP SDK
with `pip install 'lgtmaybe[mcp]'`. The Homebrew formula and Windows executable
do not include it. See
[Use from a coding agent over MCP](use-from-a-coding-agent-over-mcp.md).

## Configure a Provider

lgtmaybe has no built-in model, so tell it which provider and model to use
once:

```bash
lgtmaybe config init
```

It looks for a provider API key in your environment (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ZAI_API_KEY`), Azure, AWS or Google
Cloud credentials, and a running ollama with its pulled models. It offers the
first one it finds, suggests a current model, then checks the pair with one
tiny request so a wrong key or model fails now rather than mid-review. It
writes the provider and model to `~/.config/lgtmaybe/config.yml`; API keys stay
in your environment and are never written. Pass `--no-verify` to skip the
check, for example when you are offline.

Until a provider is configured (by `config init`, a `.lgtmaybe.yml`, or
`--provider`/`--model`), `lgtmaybe review` stops at once with a pointer to
`config init` instead of guessing a model.

## Next Steps

- Run your first local review: [Getting started](../tutorial/getting-started.md).
- Diagram what a change touches: [Generate a change overview](generate-a-change-diagram.md).
- Post reviews on real pull requests: [Use as a GitHub Action](use-as-github-action.md).

# Choose a Review Model

**Start with `google/gemini-3.8-flash` on OpenRouter.** In the 24 September
2026 benchmark on lgtmaybe 2.8.5, it led the 11 tested models on both small,
varied changes (60.9%) and large Python diffs (71.4%), and its breadth result
is fully adjudicated. It still flagged findings on seven of nine clean changes,
so check its output before acting on it.

```bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...
lgtmaybe review --provider openrouter --model google/gemini-3.8-flash
```

If large diffs matter more than small changes, consider `openai/gpt-6-luna`. It
was second on long horizon (64.6%) and finished those five cases in 440 seconds
of total review time, against Gemini's 798. Its breadth recall was much lower
(42.9% against 62.9%), so it is not the everyday default.

These recommendations come from a synthetic corpus, not your repository. Try
the candidates on recent pull requests before choosing a team default. See [Review with OpenRouter](review-with-openrouter.md) for setup.

## What the Suites Measure

- **Breadth:** 32 small changes across seven programming languages, GitHub
  Actions, and Terraform, with 72 planted findings and nine verified-clean
  changes. Each model reviews the suite three times; the table reports the
  median result.
- **Long horizon:** Four increasingly large Python changes with eight planted
  bugs each, plus one large clean change. Each model reviews the suite once.

The suites use different cases, so **compare scores within a suite, never
across suites.** Score is closed-world F0.5, which weights precision above
recall, multiplied by completeness: the share of review calls that returned
parseable findings. An unmatched finding counts as a false positive even if it
might be useful on real code. A provisional breadth score still has a few
findings awaiting human adjudication.

## Cloud Models Tested on lgtmaybe 2.8.5

### Small Changes: Breadth

| Model | Score | Recall | Precision | False positives | Clean pass |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | **60.9%** | 62.9% | 79.3% | 12 | 22.2% |
| `x-ai/grok-4.7` † | 55.7% | 62.9% | 70.1% | 20 | 11.1% |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` † | 55.1% | 62.9% | 70.0% | 21 | 11.1% |
| `moonshotai/kimi-k3` † | 52.0% | 65.7% | 63.3% | 27 | 0.0% |
| `openai/gpt-6-sol` | 50.0% | 60.0% | 62.9% | 26 | 11.1% |
| `openai/gpt-6-luna` † | 50.0% | 42.9% | 70.5% | 13 | 22.2% |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3` † | 49.9% | 64.3% | 67.6% | 22 | 11.1% |
| `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash` † | 46.2% | 62.9% | 61.3% | 29 | 0.0% |
| `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` † | 45.4% | 62.9% | 59.5% | 32 | 11.1% |
| `openai/gpt-6-astra` | 27.7% | 44.3% | 66.7% | 16 | 44.4% |
| `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` | 6.0% | 1.4% | 100.0% | 0 | 100.0% |

† Provisional: some borderline findings remain unadjudicated. Clean pass is
the share of nine clean changes on which the model returned no findings. Opus's
perfect precision and clean pass came from finding almost none of the planted
bugs. Astra's score was limited in part by 45.3% completeness.

### Large Diffs: Long Horizon

| Model | Score | Recall | Precision | False positives |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | **71.4%** | 87.5% | 75.7% | 9 |
| `openai/gpt-6-luna` | 64.6% | 84.4% | 69.2% | 12 |
| `openai/gpt-6-sol` | 30.6% | 78.1% | 29.8% | 59 |
| `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | 30.4% | 100.0% | 37.6% | 53 |
| `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` | 28.3% | 78.1% | 58.1% | 18 |
| `openai/gpt-6-astra` | 25.5% | 56.2% | 40.0% | 27 |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | 24.3% | 59.4% | 48.7% | 20 |
| `x-ai/grok-4.7` | 21.9% | 65.6% | 36.2% | 37 |
| `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash` | 21.5% | 71.9% | 44.2% | 29 |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3` | 8.1% | 81.2% | 12.4% | 183 |
| `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` | 0.0% | 0.0% | 100.0% | 0 |

Kimi found all 32 planted bugs but added 53 false positives. The low scores
for Qwen Flash and Xiaomi also reflect completeness below 50%: many of their
review calls produced no parseable findings. The [benchmark results][results] show
per-case recall, token use, truncation, and wall time.

## Local Models

The published local runs used older lgtmaybe versions and have not been
repeated on 2.8.5. Among local models with canonical runs on both suites,
`nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` is the strongest: 48.2% breadth on 2.2.0 and
43.8% long horizon on 2.1.4. Treat those numbers as a starting point for a
local trial, not a comparison with the cloud tables above. The example below
reaches it through a local OpenAI-compatible server such as vLLM:

```bash
lgtmaybe review \
  --provider openai-compatible \
  --model nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --api-base http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
```

See [Run locally with ollama](run-locally-with-ollama.md) for hardware guidance
and [Other OpenAI-compatible servers](use-a-custom-openai-compatible-endpoint.md)
for vLLM, llama.cpp, and LM Studio setup.

## Source and Limits

The [benchmark repository][bench] holds the live leaderboard, [complete
results][results], reproducible commands, and append-only raw results. Older
runs stay there for historical comparison, but their model versions, lgtmaybe
versions, and sometimes review profiles differ. The cloud recommendations on
this page use the 22 canonical runs from 24 September 2026 (11 models, two
suites).

The corpus is synthetic and does not measure provider price, availability,
data handling, or performance on your codebase. No run in this cohort has an
immutable audit trace; the live leaderboard reports audit availability.

[bench]: https://github.com/MattJColes/lgtmaybe-benchmarks
[results]: https://github.com/MattJColes/lgtmaybe-benchmarks/blob/main/RESULTS.md

# Use lgtmaybe as a GitHub Action

This guide adds lgtmaybe to a repository as a GitHub Actions workflow. The
workflow reviews every pull request (PR) automatically.

!!! tip "Not on GitHub?"

    lgtmaybe runs the same review on GitLab and Gitea. See
    [Review on GitLab](./review-on-gitlab.md) or
    [Review on Gitea](./review-on-gitea.md).

lgtmaybe is listed on the
[GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/lgtmaybe). It is a
**GitHub Action**: the reviewer runs in your workflow. Its
[provider](../reference/glossary.md#provider), model and provider credentials go in the step's
`with:` block.

Reviews post as `github-actions[bot]` using the workflow's own token. To post
as `lgtmaybe[bot]` instead, install the public lgtmaybe App and set
`github_identity: lgtmaybe`. The App changes only the comment author.

The [minimal OpenAI workflow](#minimal-workflow-openai) below shows the complete
default setup.
[`examples/workflows/`](https://github.com/MattJColes/lgtmaybe/tree/main/examples/workflows)
has a ready-to-copy workflow for every cloud and API-key provider.

Alongside the review, lgtmaybe posts a
[change overview](../reference/glossary.md#change-overview) comment on opened, reopened,
pushed-to and retargeted pull requests (`auto_diagram`, on by default). It holds:

- a description;
- a [risk-of-change](../reference/glossary.md#risk-of-change) rating;
- a **[High Impact Areas](../reference/glossary.md#high-impact-areas)** section;
- a Mermaid flowchart, plus a sequence diagram when the change alters a
  run-time flow.

Each push refreshes it. Set `auto_diagram: false` for no overview. To drop one
section, set `auto_describe: false`, `high_impact: false` or `risk: false`.

lgtmaybe skips the automatic overview when a Mermaid diagram is already there,
in the PR description or in a comment lgtmaybe didn't post. The review summary
says so. `/diagram` still posts one on request.

ollama runs the model on your own machine, so use it through the
[CLI](run-locally-with-ollama.md) rather than a posting workflow.

## Security Requirement: pull_request_target

All lgtmaybe workflows use the `pull_request_target` trigger, not
`pull_request`. This is non-negotiable:

- `pull_request_target` runs in the context of the **base branch** (the
  branch the PR merges into), so it can read secrets and write to the PR.
- lgtmaybe **never checks out or runs PR code**. It fetches the
  [diff](../reference/glossary.md#diff) through the GitHub API, so the PR author cannot get code to
  run in the reviewer's environment.

The action reads the PR from the triggering event, so there is no PR URL input
to set. On an `issue_comment` event it runs the slash command (`/review`,
`/improve`, `/ask`, `/describe`, `/diagram`) through the same engine.

On a `synchronize` push (new commits on the PR), the review is
**[incremental](../reference/glossary.md#incremental-review)** by default. lgtmaybe reviews only the
commits added since the last completed review. Earlier
[findings](../reference/glossary.md#finding) stay open until fixed. Comment `/review full` for a
full re-review, or pin the behaviour with the `incremental` input or config key.

Replies inside finding threads do not trigger lgtmaybe. A reply is not evidence
that a finding is fixed, so push the fix instead. lgtmaybe resolves the thread
and replies `✅ Looks resolved.` once both of these are true:

- the next review no longer reports the finding;
- GitHub marks the thread outdated.

Use `/ask` when you want the model to answer a question.

> **Upgrading:** lgtmaybe no longer has the `answer_replies` option. Delete it
> from `.lgtmaybe.yml` (configuration is strict, so a leftover key is an error)
> and from your Action inputs. Also remove the `pull_request_review_comment`
> trigger from custom workflows.

> **Note on cost.** With ollama the model runs on your own hardware, so reviews
> are free. On a hosted provider each run uses tokens you pay for, so decide
> who can trigger one (next section). The default limits that to people you
> trust. `max_files` (in `.lgtmaybe.yml`) and `max_input_tokens` keep any single
> run modest.

## Who Can Trigger a Review

You choose who reviews run for. The example workflows gate the `review` job on
the triggering user's
[author association](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/enums#commentauthorassociation):
GitHub's label for how that user relates to the repository. They default to
**trusted contributors**: `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, and `COLLABORATOR`.

A maintainer can still review an outside contributor's PR at any time by
commenting `/review` on it. The maintainer's own association passes the gate.

The same `if:` also requires a comment to carry a slash command before any job
starts. `issue_comment` fires on every comment on every pull request. Without
that clause, an ordinary "lgtm, merging" would claim a runner, pull the
container and start Python, only to find no command and exit. That spends no
tokens, but it queues a job ahead of reviews that have work to do.

The check is substring-based and case-insensitive, so `/REVIEW` and
`/review full` both pass.

To change the policy, edit the `if:` on the `review` job:

- **Everyone:** drop the author-association checks so any PR or slash command
  runs a review. Keep the slash-command clause, or every comment starts a job.
  This suits an open project, but on a hosted provider it means anyone can
  start a paid run.
- **Returning contributors too:** add `CONTRIBUTOR` to also auto-review anyone
  who has committed to the repository before.
- **Admins only:** keep only `OWNER` (plus `MEMBER` for your organisation).

For extra guardrails, require approval for fork-PR workflow runs in
**Settings → Actions → General → Fork pull request workflows**. You can also
move the provider key behind a protected `environment`.
[Trust and Cost](../explanation/trust-and-cost.md) explains the reasoning
behind these options.

## Minimal Workflow: openai

```yaml
name: lgtmaybe

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

# One run per PR and event type: a new push cancels an in-flight review, but
# the overview's own issue_comment event cannot cancel the review that posted it.
# A title or description edit gets a group of its own, so it cancels nothing.
concurrency:
  group: lgtmaybe-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}-${{ github.event_name }}${{ github.event.action == 'edited' && !github.event.changes.base && format('-{0}', github.run_id) || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  review:
    # Only trusted authors (owner / member / collaborator) can trigger a review,
    # and a comment only starts a job when it carries a slash command.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' &&
       (github.event.action != 'edited' || github.event.changes.base) &&
       contains(fromJson('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association)) ||
      (github.event.issue.pull_request &&
       contains(fromJson('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association) &&
       (contains(github.event.comment.body, '/review') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/improve') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/ask') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/describe') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/diagram')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7 # base repo only, for .lgtmaybe.yml
      - uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
        with:
          provider: openai
          model: gpt-5.5
          api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
```

What each part does:

- `on:` runs the job when a PR is opened, reopened, pushed to or moved onto
  another base branch (`pull_request_target`), and when someone posts a comment
  (`issue_comment`). The move matters for
  [stacked pull requests](review-stacked-pull-requests.md). The `edited` event
  also fires for a new title or description, so the `if:` below skips any edit
  that leaves the base branch alone.
- `permissions:` lets the job read the repository and write review comments on
  the PR.
- `concurrency:` keeps one run per PR and event type. A new push cancels an
  in-flight review. The cancelled review gets up to 60 seconds to post what it
  already found, then it is stopped.
- `if:` is the trust gate described in
  [Who Can Trigger a Review](#who-can-trigger-a-review).
- `actions/checkout` checks out the base repo only, so lgtmaybe can read your
  `.lgtmaybe.yml`.
- `api_key` reads the `OPENAI_API_KEY` repository secret.

## Choose the GitHub Author

The minimal workflow uses GitHub's built-in workflow token and posts as
`github-actions[bot]`. This is the default and needs no App installation.

To post as `lgtmaybe[bot]`:

1. Install the public lgtmaybe App on selected repositories.
2. Add `id-token: write` to the workflow.
3. Set `github_identity: lgtmaybe`.

The provider, model, and provider key stay where they are. [Post as lgtmaybe[bot]](./post-as-a-github-app.md) has the complete
workflow, the permission boundary, and uninstall instructions.

If your organisation runs its own GitHub App, the same guide covers the
advanced `app_id` / `app_private_key` inputs.

## Other Key-Based Providers

Swap the `provider`, `model`, and `api_key` inputs:

```yaml
# anthropic
- uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
  with:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-4-6
    api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}

# openrouter
- uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
  with:
    provider: openrouter
    model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
    api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

# zai (GLM / Zhipu AI)
- uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
  with:
    provider: zai
    model: glm-4.6
    api_key: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }}

# openai-compatible (here DeepSeek's hosted API)
- uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
  with:
    provider: openai-compatible
    model: deepseek-chat
    api_base: https://api.deepseek.com/v1
    api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY }}
```

For each one:

1. Create an API key in the provider's console.
2. Add it as a repository secret
   (**Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**).
3. Reference it as `api_key`.

## Keyless Cloud Workflows

Bedrock (AWS [OIDC](../reference/glossary.md#oidc)), Vertex (GCP [WIF](../reference/glossary.md#wif)), and Azure
(Entra OIDC) need **no API keys in secrets**. Pass `aws_role_arn`,
`gcp_wif_provider`, or `azure_client_id`, and the action performs the keyless
token exchange for you. All three need the `id-token: write` permission. See:

- [Review with Bedrock OIDC](./review-with-bedrock-oidc.md)
- [Review with Vertex WIF](./review-with-vertex-wif.md)
- [Review with Azure OpenAI](./review-with-azure.md)

## Action Inputs

Every input is optional. Leave one empty to use the default shown. Most review
settings can also go in `.lgtmaybe.yml`; an input you set overrides the file.

### Provider and Model

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | none | One of `openai`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `zai`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `azure`, `ollama`, `openai-compatible` |
| `model` | none | Model identifier for the chosen provider |
| `api_key` | none | API key for key-based providers, including hosted `openai-compatible` endpoints. Leave empty for bedrock, vertex, ollama, keyless azure, and keyless local servers |
| `api_base` | none | Resource endpoint for azure (`https://<resource>.openai.azure.com`), the `/v1` base for `openai-compatible` (for example `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`), or a custom base URL for another provider |
| `fallback_model` | none | Model to re-run a call on when `model` cannot answer it. For a truncated reply it is the *last* remedy, tried only after a smaller payload, a lower `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning switched off have failed on `model`; for any other failure lgtmaybe switches to it straight away. Overrides `fallback_model` in `.lgtmaybe.yml`. See [Configure fallback_model](configure-lgtmaybe-yml.md#fallback_model) for provider scope, cost, and failure behaviour |
| `triage_model` | none (no triage) | Cheap model that runs first to skip plainly non-substantive files and rank the rest by risk. Security-relevant files always escalate past triage |
| `reflect_model` | `model` | Model for the [self-reflection](../reference/glossary.md#reflection) (false-positive audit) pass. Point it at a stronger model to audit a weaker reviewer's findings |
| `language` | English | Human language for finding titles and bodies and the describe/diagram text (for example `Japanese`). Paths, severities, and suggested code are unchanged |

### What Runs

These inputs choose what the review does. A [lens](../reference/glossary.md#lens) is one focused
review question for the model, such as security or correctness. The
[preset](../reference/glossary.md#preset) sets how many model calls the lenses take.

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` | `fast` | `fast` runs five calls (security, correctness, code health, artefacts for tests and documentation, and architecture) on every provider; `full` runs one call per lens. An explicit `categories` list in `.lgtmaybe.yml` overrides it |
| `incremental` | auto | Review only the commits added since the last completed review on `synchronize` pushes, and the whole PR elsewhere. `true`/`false` forces it. Falls back to a full review after a force-push or when there is no earlier review. A push that only moves the PR onto a new base, leaving its diff unchanged, is skipped. A retargeted PR gets a full review. `/review full` forces a full re-review on demand |
| `recursive` | `true` | Review a file whose diff exceeds `max_input_tokens` [hunk](../reference/glossary.md#hunk) by hunk instead of sending it whole. Set `false` to disable |
| `spec_review` | `true` | Check the diff against a committed spec (OpenSpec, GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro). Runs only when a spec is detected and matches the PR, so a repository without specs pays nothing |
| `static_analysis` | `true` | Run deterministic tools (ruff, bandit, mypy, gitleaks, zizmor, ast-grep, osv-scanner, semgrep) in a sandbox with no network over the changed files. Every tool feeds the model untrusted hints to confirm or discard; set `static_analysis.tool_mode` in `.lgtmaybe.yml` to make a tool post directly. Set `false` to turn it off. The image bundles every tool and an offline vulnerability database |
| `mid_review_retrieval` | `false` | Let a lens ask once for read-only files outside the diff, then re-run with them, instead of hedging a cross-file finding. Costs at most one extra call per batch and lens |
| `symbol_resolution` | `true` | During [reflection](../reference/glossary.md#reflection), use ast-grep in a read-only shallow clone of the base branch to find the definition of a symbol a finding depends on, so cross-file findings are re-judged against the real code |
| `learn_feedback` | `true` | On a re-run, suppress a finding a human reacted 👎 to on its inline comment. Resolving a thread is not a suppress signal (it means fixed) |
| `resolve_fixed` | `true` | Resolve a finding's conversation once a re-run no longer reports it and the thread is outdated. Set `false` to resolve by hand |

### What Gets Posted

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_diagram` | `true` | On an opened, reopened, pushed-to or retargeted PR, post or refresh the change overview comment. Set `false` to opt out of the whole comment |
| `auto_describe` | `true` | Head the change overview with a structured description (title, change type, summary, per-file walkthrough, intent check). Set `false` to drop the section; `/describe` still works |
| `high_impact` | `true` | Include the High Impact Areas section: infrastructure, security posture, outage risk, data migrations, backups and recovery, compatibility, observability, dependencies, cost, and compliance. Set `false` to drop the section and its model call |
| `risk` | `true` | Rate the PR's risk of change (low/medium/high/critical) from importer counts, sensitive paths, size, and untested code. Deterministic, no model call. Shown on the summary line, in the overview, as a hidden `lgtmaybe-risk` marker, and (with `pr_labels`) as a `risk/<level>` label |
| `pr_labels` | `false` | Attach derived labels: `review-effort/1-5`, `possible-security-issue`, `consider-splitting`, and `risk/<level>`. Best-effort, no extra model calls |
| `fail_on` | off | Merge-gate threshold (`info`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`critical`). Creates a `lgtmaybe` Check Run that **fails** when any finding is at or above this severity. See [Gate merges on findings](#gate-merges-on-findings) |
| `profile` | `false` | Print a timing profile in the Action log: per-stage and per-call tables with token and prompt-cache usage |

### Limits and Model Tuning

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout` | provider default (ollama/openai-compatible/openrouter 1800s, cloud 600s) | Enforced wall-clock timeout for each model call. For ollama and openai-compatible, which may be a single-slot server that queues calls, the default is multiplied by the concurrency, then capped at `max_review_seconds` but never below 1800s. Transient failures (capacity 429s, connection blips, 5xx) are retried with exponential backoff. Permanent ones (bad key, quota or billing 429, unknown model) and a call that uses up this whole timeout fail fast: re-sending the same request against the same budget would only burn it twice |
| `max_review_seconds` | `3600` | Soft wall-clock ceiling for the whole review. Once it passes, queued calls are skipped and partial results post with a notice. A cancelled or timed-out job does the same (on SIGINT/SIGTERM). `0` disables |
| `max_review_tokens` | `0` (off) | Soft ceiling on billable tokens (input plus output) across every model call. Once it passes, no further calls start and the review posts what it has with a notice. Run once with `profile: true`, read the total, then set this above it |
| `max_concurrency` | `6` | Concurrent model calls across the whole review. Set `1` for a serial local run |
| `max_input_tokens` | `100000` | Token budget per model call before the diff is split into batches. Left unset, it is lowered to fit the model's context window when that is known |
| `max_tokens` | 16384 on ollama, openai-compatible and openrouter; the model's own ceiling elsewhere | Cap on the tokens each call may generate. `0` sends no cap. OpenRouter reserves prompt plus `max_tokens` against a prepaid balance, so the finite default keeps that bounded; raise it when a long answer is being cut off |
| `max_findings_per_lens` | `50` | Ceiling on findings from one (batch, lens) call, a backstop against a degenerate reply. When it fires, the highest-severity findings are kept and the review names the lens and the count dropped. `0` disables |
| `reasoning_effort` | route default | Bound how much a reasoning model thinks per call: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `default`. Use it when lens calls truncate or run long |
| `temperature` | `0.0` | Sampling temperature (`0.0` is deterministic) |
| `num_ctx` | `32768` | ollama context window (ignored for hosted providers) |
| `structured_output` | `true` | Constrain output to the findings JSON schema via `response_format` (JSON mode). Set `false` for an `openai-compatible` gateway that rejects it |
| `repair_unparseable` | `true` | When a reply cannot be parsed, send it back once (with the schema, without the diff) to be reformatted. Costs nothing on a healthy run |
| `retry_without_schema` | `true` | If the reformat also fails, re-run that lens once without `response_format`. Only applies to calls that sent the schema |

### Cloud Auth

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `aws_role_arn` | none | IAM role ARN to assume via OIDC for bedrock (keyless) |
| `aws_region` | `us-east-1` | AWS region for bedrock |
| `gcp_wif_provider` | none | Workload Identity Federation provider resource name for vertex |
| `gcp_service_account` | none | GCP service account email to impersonate via WIF |
| `azure_client_id` | none | Entra (Azure AD) client ID with a federated credential, for keyless azure via OIDC |
| `azure_tenant_id` | none | Entra (Azure AD) tenant ID for keyless azure |

### GitHub Identity and Runtime

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config_path` | `.lgtmaybe.yml` | Path to the config file, relative to the repo root. With the default, a missing file is fine; a path you set must exist |
| `github_token` | `${{ github.token }}` | Token for reading the PR and posting the review |
| `github_identity` | `actions` | Comment author: `actions` posts as `github-actions[bot]`; `lgtmaybe` posts as `lgtmaybe[bot]` once the public App is installed and `id-token: write` is granted |
| `identity_broker_url` | managed endpoint | Advanced override for the public App identity exchange |
| `app_id` | none | Advanced: ID of your own GitHub App, used with `app_private_key`. Do not combine with `github_identity: lgtmaybe` |
| `app_private_key` | none | Advanced: private key of your own App named by `app_id` |
| `app_owner` | current repo's owner | Owner for a cross-repo App token |
| `app_repositories` | current repo | Repositories the App token may access, newline- or comma-separated. Use with `app_owner` |
| `image` | `ghcr.io/mattjcoles/lgtmaybe:v2` | Override the container image (advanced) |

The action passes `GITHUB_TOKEN` and the provider credentials into the
container itself, so you do not set them as `env`.

## Gate Merges on Findings

Set [`fail_on`](../reference/glossary.md#fail-on) to a [severity](../reference/glossary.md#severity) to turn the
review into a merge gate. After posting the review, lgtmaybe creates a
**Check Run** named `lgtmaybe`: a pass or fail result GitHub shows on the PR.
Its conclusion is `failure` when any surviving finding is at or above that
severity, and `success` otherwise. lgtmaybe never sets PR approval state, so a
clean review stays comment-only.

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  checks: write # needed to create the Check Run

# ...

- uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2
  with:
    provider: openai
    model: gpt-5.5
    api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    fail_on: high # block merge on any high/critical finding
```

To make it block merges, mark the check as required in **branch protection**:

1. Open **Settings → Branches → Branch protection rules** (or a ruleset) for the
   target branch.
2. Enable **Require status checks to pass before merging**.
3. Search for and add the **`lgtmaybe`** check. It appears in the list once the
   Action has run with `fail_on` set on a PR against that branch.

A PR with a finding at or above the threshold then shows a failing `lgtmaybe`
check. It cannot merge until the finding is resolved, or until `fail_on` is set
to a higher severity (for example `high` to `critical`).

Leave `fail_on` unset (the default) to keep reviews advisory. lgtmaybe then
creates no check run.

Creating the Check Run requires `checks: write`, as in the snippet above. The
public `lgtmaybe[bot]` App intentionally does not hold that permission, so
`github_identity: lgtmaybe` cannot be combined with `fail_on`. Use the default
Actions identity or a self-managed App granted `Checks: write`.

### What the Public App Cannot Do

The public `lgtmaybe[bot]` App holds a deliberately minimal permission set, so
two features are unavailable under `github_identity: lgtmaybe`:

| Feature | Behaviour under the public App |
|---|---|
| `fail_on` (merge-gate Check Run) | Refused up front with a setup error, because it needs `checks: write` |
| `resolve_fixed` (auto-resolve fixed conversations) | GitHub refuses `resolveReviewThread`, so threads stay open. The review is unaffected: nothing is posted to the thread, the refusal is logged once with what to do, and the run continues |

Both work under the default `actions` identity (with `pull-requests: write` in
the workflow `permissions:` block) or a self-managed App holding the matching
permission. Set `resolve_fixed: false` to stop attempting it.

## Adding a Config File

Place a `.lgtmaybe.yml` at the repo root to control severity thresholds, path
filters, file caps, and more. Set `config_path` if it lives elsewhere.
[Configure .lgtmaybe.yml](./configure-lgtmaybe-yml.md) lists all options.

## Pin to a Specific Version

`@v2` is a floating tag: it tracks the latest `v2.x.x` release. To pin the
action exactly, use a full version tag:

```yaml
uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2.11.1
```

The action's default `image` is the floating `ghcr.io/mattjcoles/lgtmaybe:v2`.
Pinning the tag alone therefore still runs the newest v2 container. To pin the
reviewer too, set the image to the matching version tag (no `v` prefix):

```yaml
uses: MattJColes/lgtmaybe@v2.11.1
with:
  image: ghcr.io/mattjcoles/lgtmaybe:2.11.1
  # ...provider, model, api_key as usual
```

## On Another Code Host

The review is identical on GitLab and Gitea. Only the wiring and a few
differences in what each [code host](../reference/glossary.md#code-host) supports change:

- [Review on GitLab](./review-on-gitlab.md): a CI job running
  `lgtmaybe gitlab-ci` on merge request pipelines.
- [Review on Gitea](./review-on-gitea.md): Gitea Actions, running the same
  container as GitHub.

Keyless cloud auth (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure) relies on GitHub Actions' OIDC
token, so it is available only on GitHub. On the other hosts use an API-key
provider or `ollama`.
